trust_decision.summary: During OAuth discovery the client decides whether a fetched RFC 9728 protected-resource-metadata document is authoritative for this MCP resource: the document's `resource` field must be present and identify `self.base_url` (root-identifier trailing-slash tolerated, path identifiers compared exactly), otherwise discovery fails with MetadataError instead of following the document's `authorization_servers`.

landing_point.why: An engineer reading only 'missing resource field validation in OAuth Protected Resource Metadata discovery' looks at the one place that fetches and consumes the protected-resource metadata document (discover_oauth_server_via_resource_metadata), where authorization_servers/scopes_supported are taken from the fetched JSON at lines 1842-1890.

fix_sites.module_kind: OAuth client discovery helper (private async fn in transport/auth)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can leave the non-string-`resource` route (and any other malformed-metadata shape) alone by arguing the codebase deliberately treats unparseable protected-resource metadata as a soft error and falls through to direct authorization-server discovery, so shape-invalid documents are 'already handled' by the compatibility path.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Protected-resource metadata is legitimately served at path-inserted well-known locations (/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/<path> and /<path>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource) for servers whose base URL has a path; a fix that compares the document's `resource` to the metadata document URL, or that rejects any non-identical string, breaks those legitimate deployments.

O6_input_shapes: `resource` string exactly equal to base_url -> accepted
root identifier with/without trailing slash in either direction (https://h vs https://h/) -> accepted (fix.diff:50-61, fix.diff:157-166)
non-root identifier with trailing slash (https://h/mcp vs https://h/mcp/) -> rejected (fix.diff:168-171)

`resource` present but not a JSON string (array/number/object) -> struct deserialization fails, document treated as unparseable and silently skipped (crates/rmcp/src/transport/auth.rs:1987-1993) - not handled by the fix

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Protected-resource metadata whose `resource` is a non-string JSON value makes serde reject the whole document, so fetch_resource_metadata_from_url returns Ok(None) and discovery silently falls through to direct /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server discovery instead of applying or failing the resource check.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Malformed metadata JSON is deliberately a soft error ('treat resource metadata JSON parse failure as soft error', crates/rmcp/CHANGELOG.md:86) and the fallback is documented behaviour (crates/rmcp/src/transport/auth.rs:1067-1074); a parse failure looks like any other garbage document.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~900 lines from the landing point (parser at 1987, fallback decision at 1067)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Authorization-server metadata fetched during discovery is trusted without checking that its `issuer` identifies the URL/origin it was fetched from; the issuer is only compared later against the authorization-response `iss` value.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The code explicitly tolerates servers that omit issuer data for backwards compatibility (crates/rmcp/src/transport/auth.rs:1490-1493, 1501-1503), so binding the AS-metadata issuer is a separate RFC 8414 requirement, not this advisory's protected-resource `resource` field.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~40 lines from the landing point; used at 1479-1512

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A public `set_metadata` that would also have to refuse metadata documents whose identity does not match the manager's base_url.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already exists as the documented escape hatch for callers that ran discovery themselves, so a maintainer hardening metadata trust would naturally add a validated variant next to it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An authorization-server allowlist that requires the AS to be the one advertised by this resource's own metadata, not merely a public host.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The current check only blocks private/loopback hosts; extending it is the obvious incremental hardening step in the same discovery flow.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Rejecting a caller-supplied client-credentials `resource` parameter that differs from base_url before putting it on the token request.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The token/authorization requests already hard-code `resource = self.base_url` (1310, 1558), while the client-credentials branch forwards the caller's value, so a maintainer could reasonably close that gap.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A per-candidate-path resource-identifier expectation for path-inserted well-known metadata URLs.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The three candidate paths were added for real identity providers, so a maintainer adding identity binding would plausibly thread the expected resource through well_known_paths.

O9_family: CWE-345 insufficient verification of data authenticity - OAuth protected-resource metadata resource/audience identity not bound to the MCP server URL (metadata spoofing)

O10_build.toolchain: cargo / rustc, edition 2024 workspace at Cargo.toml:11-12; affected code is behind the `auth` feature (crates/rmcp/Cargo.toml:184)
O10_build.project_tests: Unit tests in crates/rmcp/src/transport/auth.rs (`mod tests`, e.g. custom_http_client_handles_protected_resource_discovery at 3179, protected_resource_metadata_rejects_private_authorization_server_urls at 3304) using an in-process RecordingOAuthHttpClient; integration test crates/rmcp/tests/test_client_credentials.rs runs a local axum mock server on 127.0.0.1 (required-features auth, crates/rmcp/Cargo.toml:328-331). No external network or services needed.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `resource: Option<String>` to ResourceServerMetadata and error unless it equals base_url by plain string equality (or compare it to the metadata document URL), then update the two existing discovery tests.

out_of_scope_notes: Noted but not pursued: the same-origin-only check on the WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata URL (crates/rmcp/src/transport/auth.rs:900-923) also permits a same-origin but different path than base_url; that is the condition the published resource binding closes, so it is inside this advisory's scope and is not reported as a separate issue.
